_meta.purpose: MOBILE-PREVIEW-4 (AWJ_APP_BUILDER_REAL_MOBILE_PREVIEW_HORIZON.md) — canonical, single-source conformance fixture for the App Builder action-decode and navigation-support contract. Both the Flutter runtime's implementation (source of truth) and the Builder web Preview's derived TypeScript port MUST agree on every case's 'decode' result, and — for 'navigate' actions only — on whether the real shipped runtime's RuntimeActionHandler actually changes screen for that pageId. This file is the one place that contract is written down; do not duplicate case data inline in either test suite.
sourceOfTruth: mobile/lib/actions/app_action.dart (decodeAction — param validation per action type)
_meta.note: Every case's 'decode' field is a real cross-runtime invariant: decodeAction's param validation is identical Dart/TypeScript logic and must produce the same typed result (or null) on both sides for the same ActionRef. The 'previewOutcome' field is NOT a Flutter concept — the shipped runtime has no 'outcome classification', it just dispatches for real (a live network call, a real screen switch, or a real silent no-op). It is Browser-Preview-only policy layered on top of the identical decode step, describing what Browser Preview honestly shows since it has no live commerce/auth. Its 'navigate'/'navigate-unsupported' split IS still a real cross-runtime fact (mirrors onNavigate's exact pageId switch — only 'home'/'cart' change RuntimeState.page, anything else is a documented no-op — 'a schema-authoring mistake, not a runtime crash'), so the Dart consumer asserts it too, by actually dispatching through RuntimeActionHandler and checking RuntimeState.page. 'requires-live-data' (openProduct/addToCart/updateCartQuantity/removeCartItem) and 'safe-noop' (refresh) are preview-only judgments about whether the action needs a live network/auth boundary Browser Preview intentionally does not have (openProduct's OWN action-handler call is instant/local — the live dependency is the destination Product screen's own CommerceClient fetch, not the navigate step itself) — the Dart consumer does not assert these two categories, since Flutter has nothing analogous to 'this action is unavailable in preview' to check.

cases.description: navigate({pageId:'home'}) decodes and is one of the runtime's exact two wired navigation targets — RuntimeActionHandler.onNavigate switches RuntimeState.page to home.
navigate({pageId:'cart'}) — the runtime's other wired navigation target.

navigate({pageId:'categories'}) decodes fine (well-formed ActionRef) but RuntimeActionHandler.onNavigate's switch has no case for it — the real shipped app does nothing at all. Not a Preview gap to paper over by inventing a generic page router.
navigate({}) — decodeAction returns null (fail-safe, never throws); dispatcher does nothing.
navigate({pageId:42}) — pageId must be a String.

openProduct always decodes for any non-empty productId and (on real mobile) always switches RuntimeState.page to product — but the destination ProductScreen fetches the product from CommerceClient, which Browser Preview has no live/authorized path to.
addToCart with only productId — quantity defaults to 1, variantId to null.
quantity must be a positive int when present.
quantity 0 decodes fine — removal-by-zero is the caller's policy, not decodeAction's.

refresh decodes regardless of params and, on real mobile, only bumps a local refresh counter — no network call at all (proven by mobile/test/app/runtime_action_handler_test.dart's 'onRefresh ... without touching the Commerce API'). Safe to treat as a real no-op in Preview too: there is nothing live to refresh.
